title: Heuristic kernel scorer and prefill/decode pacing for FlashAttention v3 integration
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Goal: Integrate FlashAttention v3 into the serving runtime with a heuristic-based kernel scoring function that chooses between FlashAttention v2/v3 variants and safe fallbacks at prefill and decode time. The scorer should account for sequence distribution, batch shape, memory head occupancy, and observed numerical stability for mixed-precision paths. This ticket covers design, experiment harness, telemetry, feature flags, and a rollbackable rollout plan.

Motivation: v3 offers better latency for long sequences on A100/RTX-class GPUs but has regressions for short sequences and some mixed-precision kernels produce occasional NaNs on pathological prompt shapes. Previous attempts (see ENG-4721, ENG-9932) showed opportunity but also flakiness when the scheduler aggressively selects v3. We need a middle-ground: a deterministic scoring function that is stable across noisy telemetry and is easy to update from runtime release flags.

Success criteria:
- Mean token latency reduction >= 8% on long-seq 8xA100 nightly benchmark (95% CI) with <= 1% regression on short-seq workloads.
- No increase in spurious NaN/inf generation beyond baseline in 30-day canary traffic.
- Clear telemetry: kernel_choice_score KPI and prefill/decode latency histograms available in Console runtime-2025.02 dashboard.
- Rollout via feature flag with automatic throttled ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and immediate rollback on NaN spike or >3% p95 latency regression for consumer-tier endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: Heuristic scorer implemented and behind runtime feature flag
Integration tests covering prefills with seq lens [16, 128, 512, 2048] and batch sizes [1,4,16] pass in CI
Nightly perf job shows long-seq p50 improvement and short-seq within regression budget
Telemetry events kernel_choice and kernel_reason emitted for each request
Rollout plan doc and rollback runbook added to Confluence
steps: Design scorer: initial weighted score function (hardware_pref * model_pref * seq_factor * numerics_penalty)
Add telemetry hooks for kernel_choice, kernel_score_components, and fallback_reason
Implement feature-flagged selection in serving runtime (prefill fast path, decode path)
Create CI job with synthetic prompt shapes and run on v2/v3 images
Run canary on 10% internal accounts for 72 hours, collect NaN counts and latency deltas
Ramp rollout if canary passes, otherwise revert feature flag and collect debug dumps
comments: 2025-01-28 | Avery Chen: Kicked off spike. Collected initial microbenchmarks comparing fa2/fa3 on p4d/ga100 at sequence lengths 64/512/2048. Results attached. Short seq (<=64) shows fa2 slightly faster due to lower kernel invocation overhead. fa3 dominates for >=1024. See GH-PR 12034 for raw harness.

2025-01-30 | Priya Nair: Drafted heuristic. Proposing a base score computed as: hw_weight*(is_ga100?1.2:1.0) + seq_weight*(seq_len_norm) - numeric_risk_penalty. numeric_risk_penalty derived from historical NaN rates per model family. Request feedback from Samir on how to expose numeric risk metadata on model manifest.

2025-02-03 | Samir Patel: Reviewed heuristic. Suggest using 95th percentile occupancy instead of mean for seq_factor to avoid mis-prediction on heavy tails. Also recommend a small hysteresis when switching kernels across sequential tokens to avoid oscillation during decode (sticky selection for N tokens).

2025-02-05 | Diego Martinez: Implemented telemetry events 'kernel_choice' and 'kernel_score_components' in runtime branch feature/kernel-scorer. Pushed internal PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12345. Added unit tests for component serialization. CI running on cuda-12-image.

2025-02-08 | Priya Nair: Canary started on 10 internal customers. Early telemetry: kernel_choice shows 62% fa3 for seq>=1024, 8% fa3 for seq<=64. Observed 0.3% NaN rate spike in one customer for a GPT2-small variant — investigating whether it's a numerics issue or instrumentation artifact. Captured device-side debug dumps (nvprof traces) and attached to the incident ticket.

2025-02-11 | Avery Chen: Reproduced NaN on local with mixed-precision calling pattern and stray attention mask edge-case. Mitigation: add numeric_risk_penalty override that forces v2 for models with known instabilities discovered by failing tests. Preparing small patch to make the override configurable via model manifest label 'attention:stable-v3=false'

2025-02-12 | Priya Nair: Updated rollout plan and added automatic rollback rule: if canary NaN rate > 0.5% absolute increase or p95 latency regresses > 3% for 30 minutes, disable feature flag. Patch landed in PR 12382 that reads model labels from manifest and enforces stable-v3=false fallback. Next: expand CI coverage and schedule a full-nightly run for cross-GPU validation.
